name: Big box retail
summary: Single-tenant 50,000–200,000 SF store: tilt-up or CMU walls, steel joist roof, large clear spans, loading docks and a big parking field. Very price-efficient per SF; retailer prototypes drive scope. Evidence is thin (RSMeans department-store model and national retail quartiles); value is a reasoned derivation.

typicalSize.method: Catalog definition (50k–200k SF); RSMeans department store model uses 110,000 SF (e1).

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Derived: FAR ≈ 0.2–0.3 with 4–5 spaces/1,000 SF and truck court.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per GSF (judgment; big-box retailers typically 4–5/1,000).

perPrimaryUnit.method: RSMeans 2019 1-story department store (110,000 SF, complete basic building, excl. site) $113.46–123.00 (e1) × ≈1.3 = $147–160; + sitework ≈$25–35/SF for 4–5/1,000 parking and truck court (Kirksey one-story 5/1,000 sitework $16–37, e6) → ≈$175–190. Mid = $180. Low = $130 ≈ RSMeans retail 1/4 quartile ($96, 2022, e2) escalated + site. High = $260 ≈ RLB strip Dallas high ($270, e4) — big boxes rarely exceed small-shop strip costs. RSMeans model escalation 2019→2026 ≈ ×1.3, inferred from RSMeans' own office 2–4 story model: 2019 total $187.02 (open) / $204.43 (union) vs. 2026 national $253.63 (BD+C) = ×1.24–1.36. This is only used to compare evidence; the build script escalates from the stated dollarYear.

scope.notes: Complete building delivered to the retailer (basic finishes and MEP) plus on-site work; excludes store fixtures/racking, refrigeration, land, soft costs, off-site road improvements.

systemSplit.method: Derived. MEP from RSMeans 2022 retail medians (plumbing 5.45%, mechanical 6.15%, electrical 11.25%, e2) adjusted for a large open box (ESFR sprinklers 21 3%). Sitework 20%. Structure/envelope (tilt-up 03, joists/deck 05, roofing 07) by judgment.

cost.method: Derived judgment per dock position: pit leveler + seal + insulated overhead door + bumpers.

lineItems.name: On-site work incl. parking field and truck court (carve-out)

cost.method: Derived: 20% of mid; Kirksey one-story 5/1,000 sitework $16–37/SF (e6) plus truck court and detention.
From _blocks/energy.json rooftop-solar-commercial; qty ≈ 5 W per SF of roof (judgment).

pctOfHard.method: Derived: prototype designs keep A/E at 4–6% (RSMeans department store model carries 6%); permits/platting 1–2%, survey/geotech 1%, insurance/legal 2%, developer fee 2–4%.

softCosts.notes: Build-to-suit for a credit tenant typically carries low leasing cost.

design.method: Simple commercial shells: low design contingency.

source.title: Construction Cost Estimates for a Store, Department, 1 Story in National, US (2019 RSMeans data)

evidence.scopeNotes: Basic-component model building, excludes sitework. Hard = SubTotal + contractor fees (open $113.46, union $123.00); architectural fee 6% excluded.

source.title: North America Quarterly Construction Cost Report, Q3 2026 (Indicative Construction Costs table)

evidence.quote: Indicative construction costs, Retail Shopping — Strip: Dallas 200–270; Phoenix 135–220; Charlotte 205–290 (USD/SF GFA, hard construction costs).
evidence.scopeNotes: Values are the Dallas column; Phoenix 135–220; 18-US-city median 202.5–295. RLB does not say whether strip figures are shell-only or include sitework.

evidence.quote: Square Foot Costs: Office Building, 2-4 Story — National Average Q2 2026 $253.63.
evidence.scopeNotes: Used only to infer RSMeans model escalation 2019→2026 (vs. 2019 office 2–4 story model total $187.02–204.43).

evidence.quote: ONE-STORY FLEX OFFICE BUILDINGS $103 to $122/SF ... Cost includes $16 to $22/sf for sitework, assuming five spaces/1,000 sf in a surface parking lot.
evidence.scopeNotes: One-story building with 5/1,000 surface parking — closest published proxy for retail sitework per building SF (Austin $21–30, Dallas $23–37 for the same building).

openQuestions: Only an RSMeans 2019 department-store model was retrievable; a recent public big-box development agreement or TIF budget would validate the mid.
